Your urinalysis is normal, but your ESR is elevated, indicating inflammation despite your ANA being negative and chest X-ray being clear. Given your history of arthritis management and the new onset of cough and rash, do you have any history of kidney stones, blood clots, or recent infections?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-CCP: Positive; Rheumatoid_Factor: Elevated; C-Reactive_Protein: Elevated

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rheumatoid Arthritis with extra-articular manifestations (Rheumatoid Dermatitis).

The positive Anti-CCP, elevated Rheumatoid Factor, and C-Reactive Protein, combined with your history of arthritis and new inflammatory symptoms, confirm a diagnosis of active Rheumatoid Arthritis. The rash is likely a manifestation of the systemic inflammation rather than a primary dermatological issue.
